commitResults.messageTitle: Add list command to show all games
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can add games but have no way to see what is in their
collection, so they cannot check what they own or find the number
of a game for later commands such as delete.

Let's add a ListCommand that shows every game numbered from 1, or a
short message when the collection is empty.

Like help and exit, list rejects extra arguments, so a typo such as
"list 5" is reported instead of being silently accepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command to remove a game
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot remove a game once it is added, so the collection goes
out of date when a game is sold, lost or given away.

Let's add a DeleteCommand that removes the game with the given number
from list, saves the collection, and shows the removed game.

Whether the number exists is checked when the command runs, since
only then is the size of the collection known. A number too large to
fit in an int is reported as not existing, not as "not a whole
number", so the error matches what the user actually did wrong.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add player count check to Game and GameList
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts need to find the games that suit the number of people who
turned up. The model has no way to answer that yet.

Add Game.fitsPlayerCount(), which holds the range check next to the
min and max it depends on, and GameList.filterByPlayers(), which
collects the matching games into a new list so the collection itself
is never changed by filtering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add filter command to find games by player count
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts have to scan the whole collection to work out which games
suit tonight's group.

Add FilterCommand, used as "filter COUNT", which shows only the
games whose player range includes the given count.

Let Parser.parsePlayerCount() take the command's usage string, so
the "is missing" error shows the format of the command being parsed
instead of always showing the add format.

Results are not numbered, because delete uses positions from the
full list and numbering a filtered view would be misleading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let games record an optional play time and save it
commitResults.messageBody:
Hosts want to pick games that fit the time they have tonight (#22), so a
game needs to know how long it takes. The time is optional because users
may not know it for every game.

The data file stores it as an optional 4th field (TITLE | MIN | MAX | TIME).
Old files without it still load, and an empty field also means no time,
so tags (#23) can be added as a 5th field later.

add accepts an optional /time MINUTES, and filter COUNT /time MINUTES
shows only games that take that long or less. Games with no play time
are left out, and filter says how many, so users know why a game they
expected is missing.

Prefixes are now matched only as separate words and may come in any
order, so a title such as Foo/minimal is no longer split. A repeated
prefix is rejected instead of producing a confusing error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save the game list to the data file and create it if missing
commitResults.messageBody: Storage.save() writes one game per line (TITLE | MIN | MAX) using Game.toFileString(), so the format stays in one place. It creates the data folder if needed. On startup, GameVault creates an empty data file if it does not exist. GameList.getGames() returns a read-only view so Storage can read the games. Fixes #11
